unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Chronology of 2025 Events
question:
Arrange the following major national and international events of 2025 in chronological order, from earliest to latest:

1. The grand organisation of Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj, from Makar Sankranti to Mahashivratri
2. The closing ceremony of the 38th National Games in Uttarakhand
3. The final of the ICC Champions Trophy 2025
4. The UN climate conference COP30 in Belém, Brazil

Select the correct code below.
explanation:
According to the source, the correct sequence is 1–2–3–4:
1. Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj: 13 January to 26 February 2025.
2. 38th National Games in Uttarakhand: 28 January to 14 February 2025.
3. ICC Champions Trophy 2025: 19 February to 9 March 2025.
4. UNFCCC COP30 in Belém, Brazil: scheduled for 10–21 November 2025. (Source: official 2025 programmes of the Government of India and international organisations.)

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; International Diplomacy and G20
question: Which country holds the presidency of the G20 Summit 2025, the first G20 summit hosted on the African continent?
explanation:
The source states that South Africa held the G20 presidency from 1 December 2024 to 30 November 2025. This was the first time an African country held the presidency of the G20, a major global forum. The theme of South Africa’s presidency was ‘Solidarity, Equality and Sustainable Development’, with particular attention to debt challenges in the Global South and the energy transition. (Sources cited in the source text: official G20 portal, g20.org; South African Department of International Relations.)

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Indices and Rankings
question: According to the Global Innovation Index (GII) released by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), which rank did India hold in the list of 133 economies, as stated in the source?
explanation:
The source states that India ranked 39th in the Global Innovation Index (GII) released by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), improving from 81st place in 2015. It describes India as the leading innovation economy in Central and Southern Asia and says that it had remained an ‘innovation overperformer’ among lower-middle-income economies for 14 consecutive years. Switzerland remained at the top of the ranking. (Sources cited in the source text: WIPO Global Innovation Index report; NITI Aayog’s innovation division.)

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; UNDP Human Development Report
question: According to the Human Development Report cited in the source, what was India’s rank among 193 countries, with a Human Development Index (HDI) value of 0.644?
explanation:
The source refers to UNDP’s Human Development Report titled ‘Breaking the Gridlock: Reimagining Cooperation in a Polarized World’ and states that India ranked 134th with an HDI value of 0.644, compared with 135th in 2021–22. It places India in the medium human development category and reports life expectancy at birth of 67.7 years, expected years of schooling of 12.6 years and gross national income per capita of US$6,951 in purchasing-power-parity terms. (Sources cited in the source text: UNDP Human Development Report; NITI Aayog.)

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; National Civilian Honours
question: For which kind of service is the Padma Vibhushan, India’s second-highest civilian honour, awarded among the Padma Awards announced for Republic Day 2025?
options: Only for acts of military valour during wartime
For exceptional and distinguished service in any field
Only for innovations in science and space research
Only for international peace and diplomacy
explanation:
The Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 and are among India’s highest civilian honours after the Bharat Ratna. They have three categories: Padma Vibhushan for exceptional and distinguished service (the second-highest civilian honour), Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of a high order, and Padma Shri for distinguished service. They are conferred by the President on people who have made outstanding contributions in fields such as art, literature, education, sports, medicine, social work, science and technology. (Source cited in the source text: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, official Padma Awards portal.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: No | Topic: Current affairs—national civilian honours | Level: Easy | Question Type: Direct MCQ]
verificationSource: Ministry of Home Affairs, Padma Awards portal

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Uttarakhand Uniform Civil Code
question: On which date did the Uttarakhand government formally notify the rules and launch the online registration portal for implementing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in the state?
explanation:
The Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code (Uttarakhand) Bill in February 2024, and President Droupadi Murmu gave assent on 11 March 2024. After rules were prepared by a committee chaired by retired Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai and approved by the Dhami cabinet, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami formally notified the UCC Rules and launched the citizen portal in Dehradun on 27 January 2025. The portal supports online registration relating to marriage, divorce, live-in relationships and succession. (Sources cited in the source text: Uttarakhand Home Department notification dated 27 January 2025; Department of Information and Public Relations.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Current affairs—Uttarakhand Uniform Civil Code, 2025 | Level: Moderate | Question Type: Direct MCQ]
verificationSource: Uttarakhand Home Department notification; state information department

question: What was the official mascot of the 38th National Games, held for the first time in Uttarakhand in January–February 2025?
options: ‘Mouli’ — the Himalayan monal, Uttarakhand’s state bird
explanation:
The 38th National Games were held from 28 January to 14 February 2025 in several Uttarakhand cities, including Dehradun, Haridwar, Rishikesh, Haldwani and Rudrapur. Their official mascot was ‘Mouli’, a personified representation of the colourful Himalayan monal, Uttarakhand’s state bird. The source says the host state achieved its best-ever performance at the National Games, finishing seventh in the medal table and reaching a historic total of 100 medals. (Sources cited in the source text: Indian Olympic Association; official results from Uttarakhand’s Sports Department.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Current affairs—38th National Games, Uttarakhand 2025 | Level: Easy | Question Type: Direct MCQ]
verificationSource: Indian Olympic Association; Uttarakhand Sports Department

question: What total outlay did the Uttarakhand budget for financial year 2025–26, presented by Finance Minister Prem Chand Agarwal at Bhararisain in the state’s summer capital Gairsain, exceed?
options: More than ₹1,01,000 crore, crossing the historic ₹1-lakh-crore mark
explanation:
For the first time in Uttarakhand’s budget history, the annual budget outlay crossed ₹1 lakh crore. The source gives the size of the 2025–26 budget as approximately ₹1,01,175 crore (₹1.01 lakh crore). It says special allocations were made for capital expenditure, infrastructure, tourism, reverse migration and women’s empowerment, including the Lakhpati Didi initiative. (Source cited in the source text: Uttarakhand Budget Speech 2025–26; Finance Department, Government of Uttarakhand.)

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Rishikesh–Karnaprayag Rail Project
question: In 2025, which longest railway tunnel on the 125-km Rishikesh–Karnaprayag rail project (Tunnel 8, 14.08 km long) was reported to have achieved a successful breakthrough from both ends?
options: Tunnel T-1 between Rishikesh and Shivpuri
Tunnel T-8 between Devprayag and Janasu
Tunnel T-6 between Maletha and Srinagar
Tunnel T-12 between Gauchar and Karnaprayag
explanation:
The Rishikesh–Karnaprayag broad-gauge rail line, being built by Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), is 125 km long. The source says that more than 84% of the route—about 105 km—passes through tunnels. It identifies Tunnel 8, between Devprayag and Janasu, as the project’s most challenging tunnel and one of India’s longest railway transport tunnels, at 14.08 km, and states that breakthrough from both ends was completed in 2025. (Sources cited in the source text: RVNL press release, 2025; Northern Railway.)

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; GI-Tagged Uttarakhand Products
question: Where was Uttarakhand’s first GI-tag gallery established to display and market all 27 of the state’s geographically indicated traditional products under one roof, according to the source?
explanation:
The source states that Uttarakhand obtained GI tags for a total of 27 products, including more than 18 products in a single financial year. Examples include Berinag tea, stinging-nettle fabric, jhangora, mandua, red rice, Almora bal mithai, thulma and Aipan art. It says that the Uttarakhand Rural Development Department established the state’s first dedicated GI gallery in Haldwani, Nainital district, to support protection, authentic marketing and promotion of these products. unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Uttarakhand Land Law
question: Under Uttarakhand’s stricter land-law amendments in 2025, aimed at curbing uncontrolled purchases of hill land, what restriction was introduced on outsiders buying agricultural and horticultural land?
options: A lifelong statewide ban on buying any kind of immovable property
The district magistrate-level permission route was removed, and prior government/cabinet approval plus verification of the stated purpose became mandatory
Land could be purchased only in SIDCUL industrial areas
Only residential plots up to 50 square metres could be purchased
explanation:
The source says the Uttarakhand government tightened the state’s land laws based on recommendations from the Subhash Kumar Committee and amended the Uttarakhand provisions of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950. Previously, district magistrates could permit purchases of agricultural or horticultural land of up to 12.5 acres outside municipal limits. Under the amendments described in the source, prior government/cabinet approval and verification of the land’s intended use within two years became necessary; diversion from the stated purpose could result in the land vesting in the state government. (Source cited in the source text: Uttarakhand Revenue Department orders, 2024–2025.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Current affairs—Uttarakhand land-law amendments | Level: Hard | Question Type: Direct MCQ]
verificationSource: Uttarakhand Revenue Department orders; legal provisions require factual/legal review

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Winter Char Dham Circuit
question: Under the Winter Char Dham Circuit promoted by Uttarakhand’s Tourism Department to sustain pilgrimage throughout the year, where is Kedarnath’s winter seat located and worship performed?
explanation:
During winter, heavy snowfall closes the high Himalayan Char Dham shrines, and the deities are worshipped at their designated winter seats. The source lists these locations as: Kedarnath—Omkareshwar Temple, Ukhimath (Rudraprayag); Badrinath—Narasimha Temple, Joshimath (Chamoli); Gangotri—Mukhba village, Harsil (Uttarkashi); and Yamunotri—Kharsali village (Uttarkashi). It also says the Uttarakhand government has promoted the Winter Char Dham Yatra since 2024–25 to support year-round local livelihoods. (Sources cited in the source text: Uttarakhand Tourism Development Council; Badri-Kedar Temple Committee.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Current affairs—Winter Char Dham Circuit | Level: Easy | Question Type: Direct MCQ]
verificationSource: Uttarakhand Tourism Development Council; Badri-Kedar Temple Committee

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Parvatmala Ropeway Projects
question: According to the source, what is the planned length of the modern ropeway from Sonprayag to Kedarnath, approved in 2025 under the central government’s Parvatmala project at a cost of over ₹1,200 crore, intended to reduce an eight-hour trek to about 30 minutes?
explanation:
The source gives the length of the Sonprayag–Kedarnath ropeway project as approximately 9.7 km and the cost as about ₹1,200 crore. It describes the project under Parvatmala as one of the world’s highest and longest tri-cable (3S) ropeway systems. Once completed, it is expected to reduce the difficult 16–18 km trek, which takes eight to nine hours, to a journey of approximately 30–35 minutes, with a stated capacity of 3,600 passengers per hour. (Sources cited in the source text: National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML); Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.)

unit: Unit 5: Environment and Ecology; Gross Environment Product
question: According to the source, which state became the first in India to officially adopt the Gross Environment Product (GEP) index to assess, in monetary and ecological terms, the contribution of its forests, rivers and soil to environmental conservation?
explanation:
The source identifies Uttarakhand as the first state in India to officially adopt a Gross Environment Product (GEP) index on the model of gross domestic product (GDP). Based on the concept associated with Padma Bhushan awardee Dr Anil Prakash Joshi of HESCO, the system assesses ecosystem services provided by four main ecological pillars: air quality, water recharge, soil conservation and forest cover. The stated aim is to quantify these services scientifically and in monetary terms. (Sources cited in the source text: Uttarakhand Department of Environment and Climate Change; HESCO, Dehradun.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Current affairs—Gross Environment Product index | Level: Moderate | Question Type: Direct MCQ]

unit: Unit 6: Current Affairs; Uttarakhand Women’s Empowerment Schemes
question: Which scheme run by Uttarakhand’s Women Empowerment Department provides market opportunities during major festivals for handicrafts and local products made by rural women’s self-help groups (SHGs)?
explanation:
The source says the Mukhyamantri Sashakt Bahna Utsav Yojana was launched by the Uttarakhand government to market local products made by women’s self-help groups, such as Aipan-art products, ringal handicrafts, candles, hill pulses, jute bags and organic herbal products. Under the scheme, special fairs and exhibitions are organised at block and district headquarters during major festivals, including Raksha Bandhan, Diwali, Holi and Harela. The stated goals are to strengthen rural women’s livelihoods and support the Lakhpati Didi initiative. (Source cited in the source text: government orders from the Women Empowerment and Child Development Department, Uttarakhand.)
[Uttarakhand Reference: Yes | Topic: Current affairs—Uttarakhand women’s empowerment schemes | Level: Easy | Question Type: Direct MCQ]
